## DG6 round 7 QA review: **PASS**, with no new findings

I reviewed candidate `sha256:b64b95ff…4bae` (source `70f05ed49d893378efc99cd3e1a4027fc77697e8`). The candidate ID matches over 2,750 files in the repository and in full clones. HEAD sits two commits above the source, and those commits change only delivery records.

**My open finding: F-DG6-440 (Medium) is CLOSED_VERIFIED.**
- **On the candidate:** I re-ran my round-6 reproduction on the demo stack, in en and ar, with the locale unset and with C.UTF-8. The reader who is not admitted (the Transformation Lead) now sees the same 3 totals rows as the admitted reader. The "Revenue uplift" section shows the restricted label, "No records" inside the table, and Total SAR 222,750.00 / SAR 99,000.00 Provisional. The screenshot confirms it.
- **Mutant check:** I reverted the fix in `ui.tsx`. The unit test, my probe and the in-tree e2e spec each then fail in en and ar ("TL 2 totals rows, TO 3"), so they catch the defect.

**Full review results** (every failure is disclosed in the record):
- **Static checks:** all pass. Typecheck was killed by an out-of-memory error once and passed when re-run.
- **Unit tests** (Node 22 and 24, both locale settings): all pass. In the two unset runs one test file failed because I had trimmed my clone's `docs/delivery/handbacks` to save disk space. It passes 6/6 after I restored that folder.
- **Integration**, run twice over 427 files (118 migrations, contract 932 operations, every `p6-pending` list empty): run 2 is fully green. Run 1 needed two re-runs: one after an out-of-memory crash, one after the shared disk filled up. One test, the A13 import-commit drill, then failed once because of a race in the QA test harness, not the product: `tests/qa/support/a13c.ts` checks for process exit before it checks for READY. The product result was correct, and the test passed 3/3 when run alone. This is an observation, not a finding.
- **tests/qa on its own:** 437/437 pass.
- **Product e2e:**
  - ar (unset) and both C.UTF-8 runs: 278 passed each.
  - en (unset): 3 failures. Two were 5-second waits that ran out under load, and one hit the full disk. All 23 tests in those files pass when re-run alone.
- **Root acceptance specs:** 288 passed in each locale setting. The 18 skips are the axe routes the spec marks as not scanned. The network capture shows loopback traffic only.
- **Demo stack:** 22/22 in each locale setting. The first run lost Chromium pages to memory pressure; the re-run is green.
- **a22-p6-operability, repeated 3 times:** 18/18 in each locale setting.
- **Probes:** AUD read-only, 360/390 px and 200 % text, XSS, axe and the export literals all pass. The only failures are my last-error probe, by design: it needs a17 to run first, and it passes 6/6 when it does.
- **Load and async export** (provisional, one shared host): every p95 is under 45 ms, with 0 errors. The LOAD-T20 sub-check fails as in earlier rounds because the generated data has no second user in the same scope.
- **Validators:** `--register DG6`, `--pipeline` and `--historical` for DG5 down to DG1 all pass.

**Open questions:**
- **BE-Z8:** the code is unchanged since round 6. Across 120 concurrent bursts (N = 4, 8 and 16) no occurrence was lost or double-counted.
- **BE-Z7B residuals:** items 1 to 3 are acceptable; the sweep now reports 73 operations it cannot fill. Item 4 is fixed by the F-DG6-440 repair.
- **D-219:** I found no extra disclosure. My new probe, which records every API response the screens fetch, found no restricted ids for the reader who is not admitted. Only one benefit qualified as a target, because the TL owns the demo's evidence item and created its business cases. One observation: a step owner who is not admitted can still remove a link to restricted evidence. That is an access-design question for you, not a leak.

The record is `docs/delivery/reviews/DG6/round-7/qa-verifier.json`, the verification is in `qa-verifier.verifications.json` beside it, and the evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/round-7/`. There is no findings sidecar. I removed the disposable clones.
